bull_bear.body:
- Debt-free; AGL acquisition (coloured stones) the notable inorganic move — now contributing.
- Discretionary brand investment (IPL sponsorship, leadership hires) framed as long-haul brand-building; expected to moderate.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **LGD pricing/realisation** as grower capacity doubles — mgmt insists price stable (grower margins 10–12% per IGI vs "6–10%" cited from its own deck); watch for negotiation pressure.
- **Customer concentration:** ~8–10 growers ≈ 40–50% of revenue.
- ND-jewellery softness (Q4 decline, +2% now) — mix swings dent realisation.
- Guidance (15%/20%) far below Q1 delivery (23%/29%) — either conservative or an H2 slowdown signal.
- Discretionary-spend margin drag if brand investment doesn't moderate.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, franchise-proud; CEO Tehmasp Printer strong on the certification-moat narrative, CFO Eashwar Iyer precise on the ASP/caratage and one-IGI margin mechanics. Deliberately conservative on guidance. Declined competitively sensitive detail (segment carats). Handled repeated realisation/negotiation probing patiently.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Realisation rose **despite** an LGD-heavier mix — driven by **higher caratage** (LGD stones are >1–2 carat vs sub-carat ND pointers), so ND vs LGD per-report economics effectively converge; the usual "mix dilutes ASP" fear is offset by rising stone sizes.
- The bull case is a **flywheel**: LGD's affordability creates new consumers → exposed to IGI certification → up-trade into IGI-certified natural diamonds (ND-loose global growth is the tell).
- India standalone margin (68.8%) looks "down," but that's the **one-IGI commission transfer** to overseas lead-gen offices — consolidated margin (60.4%, +270 bps) is the correct lens (mgmt insists).
- Held guidance at 15%/20% after a 23%/29% quarter — read as sandbagging or an explicit flag that H2 normalises.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The stated philosophy is 'fund growth first, then return surplus cash to shareholders — so you own a compounding business that also pays', with an explicit order of priorities: (1) reinvest in organic growth, (2) selective bolt-on M&A, (3) return surplus to shareholders, (4) maintain balance-sheet strength.
- The balance sheet is net cash of Rs. 8,005 Mn as on 31st Mar'26 and 'Effectively debt-free'; priority four is to 'Stay net-cash and keep optionality for the next opportunity'.
- Shareholder return is framed as a 'Board considered decision to balance growth & shareholder return' — no dividend policy, payout ratio or buyback is specified.
- Three reasons the model can do both are given: asset-light (little capital needed to grow), highly cash-generative (a high share of profit converts to cash the Board can allocate) and a debt-free balance sheet meaning 'returns come from strength, not borrowing'.
- Cash conversion is presented as improving: FCF/EBITDA of 50% (12M CY2023), 59% (12M CY2024) and 60% (12M CY2025), with FCF defined by the deck as operating cash flow after tax and working capital, less capex.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Scale moat: the largest laboratory and education footprint among global peers, with 36 laboratories and 21 gemology schools across 10 countries
- Brand and trust moat: over 50 years as a definitive authority in gemstone and jewelry grading; certification is described as the common language of trust in the industry
- Category leadership in lab-grown diamonds: stated No.1 position with 65% global LGD market share, and among the first organisations to certify laboratory-grown diamonds in 2005
- Domestic leadership: stated No.1 position with 50% market share in India, the world's primary diamond processing hub
- Customer entrenchment: 9 out of 10 top jewelry chains certified by IGI and more than 7,500 customers globally
- Consistency and standardisation: rigorous calibration, adherence to international standards and continual training deliver reproducible grading across global markets
- Technology-led model: skilled gemologists supported by advanced grading technology and strong IT infrastructure
- Innovation track record: first to issue jewelry identification reports in 1980
- Talent pipeline: the Schools of Gemology supply trained gemologists to the global laboratory network
- Asset-light business model with low capital requirements, zero leverage and a net cash-positive position supporting operational flexibility
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical volatility — Economic volatility, geopolitical tensions and regulatory changes could influence consumer demand and affect business performance across markets; the Company relies on its diversified geographic presence and strong industry positioning for resilience.
- Geographical revenue concentration in Gujarat and Maharashtra — A significant share of revenue is concentrated in key regions such as Gujarat and Maharashtra, exposing the business to regional economic fluctuations and industry disruptions; mitigation is expansion into new regions and global markets to diversify the customer base.
- Operational and reputational risk in grading judgment — Gem grading relies on expert judgment, so inconsistencies or errors may impact IGI's reputation and customer confidence — the core asset of a certification business; mitigated through standardized grading processes, rigorous gemologist training, AI-supported grading tools and calibrated evaluation protocols.
- Competition from global laboratories and new certification providers — Increasing competition from established global laboratories and emerging certification providers may lead to pricing pressure and market share challenges; countered by investment in advanced grading technologies, brand credibility and global expansion.
- Human resources — attracting and retaining skilled gemologists — Difficulty in attracting, training and retaining skilled gemologists could affect operational efficiency, grading accuracy and service quality; addressed through competitive compensation, career development and specialized training programmes.
- Security and insurance risk over client goods in custody and transit — Theft, fraud or damage to diamonds, jewelry and gemstones during certification or transportation could result in financial loss and reputational harm; mitigated through robust security systems, comprehensive insurance coverage and advanced tracking technologies.
- Technological risk — failure to adopt emerging grading technology — Failure to adopt emerging technologies such as advanced spectroscopy, automation or AI could affect operational efficiency, competitiveness and market positioning. The BRSR additionally flags cybersecurity and data privacy as a material risk, where threats and system vulnerabilities could compromise the security, integrity and availability of client and company data.
- Regulatory risk — licences, approvals and evolving compliance frameworks — Dependence on licences, approvals and compliance with evolving regulatory frameworks means delays or non-compliance could disrupt business operations, restrict market access and harm reputation; managed through continuous monitoring of regulatory developments, timely renewals, employee training and periodic compliance audits.

business.body:
- **Trust/network moat:** "without certification, [an LGD] can be considered just a piece of glass … IGI gives the authenticity" — certification is the indispensable trust layer.
- **Concentration cuts both ways but favours IGI:** ~10–14 large LGD growers ≈ 80% of India's grown stones (≈40–50% of IGI revenue), yet all are reliant on IGI certification → pricing has held stable (INR 80–120/carat band) for ~2 years despite scale.
- **One-IGI operating leverage:** India manufacturing/certifying strength (70–74% standalone EBITDA margin) + overseas retail lead-gen = expanding consolidated margins; interdependence is the defensible structure.
- **Only listed pure-play** certification player (declines segment carat disclosures on competitive grounds).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- The deck frames certification as the industry's missing 'trust layer' — the analogue of credit rating in banking, independent auditors in public markets, clinical testing in healthcare and quality certification in manufacturing — with IGI cast in that role for diamond and jewelry.
- Claimed market shares (deck's note: estimates as of CY25 based on value, per commissioned industry analysis, MCA filings and expert interviews) are 30-40% of global certifications, 40-50% of the India certification market and 65-75% of lab-grown diamond certifications.
- The moat is described as five traits that 'rarely coexist in one company': independent, category-agnostic, global but locally present, owner of the industry's talent pipeline, and a fifty-year legacy — with the self-reinforcing loop 'Brand strengthens trust; Trust strengthens scale; Scale reinforces leadership; Leadership strengthens the brand'.
- A 'habit of being first' is claimed at each industry inflection: founded Antwerp 1975, first to issue jewelry identification reports globally 1980, first mover in India 1999, first to certify lab-grown diamonds 2005, photoluminescence for diamond origin 2018, scaled LGD certification infrastructure 2021.
- The 21 Schools of Gemology are positioned as a strategic, self-reinforcing asset — 'a certifier that also teaches the trade owns the standard twice over — in the lab, and in the classroom' — training thousands enrolled every year toward the IGI Graduate Gemologist, described as an industry-standard credential.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] IGI acquired American Gemological Laboratories (AGL) in January 2026 — 100% of AGL Holdco Inc. acquired by IGI USA for $13.2M, against AGL turnover of $3.85M (FY24). AGL is described as pioneer of colored-stone origin determination since 1977, trusted by luxury brands, auction houses and collectors. The deck states AGL contributes incremental 3% to revenue and 2% to EBITDA for Q1FY27.
- [Ownership and listing] Blackstone acquired IGI globally in 2023; the company listed on Indian stock exchanges in 2024.
- [Reporting change] The Company has transitioned to an April–March reporting period, so FY26 (April 2025–March 2026) results are presented alongside 15M financials for January 2025–March 2026, with 15M January 2024–March 2025 as the comparative — periods in the deck are therefore not like-for-like without care.
- [Risk register] Five risks with named mitigants: LGD price pressure (revenue tracks certification volume, not stone price — volumes +20%); customer concentration (diversification across format, geography and customer type); grading consistency while scaling (blind multi-grader protocols, ISO and PwC-led audits, AI); self-certification by large retailers (co-branding at point of sale, consumer pull campaigns, raising the accreditation bar via ISO, and wiring digital certification into retailer workflows); and trade friction and demand cycles (diversified India/US/Europe/China footprint, certification being need-based across the cycle).
- [Fee economics] The certification fee is described as under 5% of retail price — 'a minimal cost on the transaction. The certificate is the reason the transaction happens' — against a retail market price band of $300-$700 versus ~$80-$120 wholesale, a 4x-6x spread.

outlook.body:
- Coloured gemstones (AGL) as a new TAM beyond diamonds; global roll-out.
- ND-loose global share gains (multiplier on realisation).

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Lead the industry's 'trust infrastructure' — position independent certification as the essential layer of confidence as consumers choose between natural and lab-grown diamonds, which management expects to coexist rather than substitute.
- Convert rising certification penetration into volume growth by leveraging deep integration across the value chain, longstanding relationships with leading growers and manufacturers, and in-factory grading capabilities that give visibility into rising certification volumes.
- Expand internationally through the AGL acquisition — combining IGI's global footprint, scale and infrastructure with AGL's scientific reputation in colored gemstone analysis, deepening presence in the United States while reinforcing linkages with India.
- Preserve acquired technical brand equity: AGL will continue to operate independently from New York under its existing leadership, retaining its methodologies while collaborating with IGI on advanced tools, reporting formats and provenance solutions.
- Invest in technology ahead of the industry — embedding advanced and AI-supported grading technologies into the science and precision of grading, authentication and certification to improve consistency and efficiency.
- Invest in people and controls — continued development of gemologists plus robust internal controls and security systems that safeguard assets and credibility.
- Pursue responsible growth through CSR initiatives that create pathways to financial independence and a more inclusive gemological ecosystem.
- Build on India as the strategic centre of gravity, positioned at the intersection of rising consumer aspirations, expanding jewelry demand and increasing emphasis on transparency and certification.
- CSR is anchored on women's empowerment through training in gemology and related skills, enabling financial independence and creating pathways to sustainable careers within the jewelry and gemological sectors.
- CSR also covers education and vocational training for underserved communities, healthcare, and environmental sustainability, with the Company adopting sustainable practices to reduce its operational impact.
- BRSR disclosures for 2025-26 are made on a standalone basis and carry Reasonable Assurance from TUV SUD South Asia Pvt. Ltd.
- Workforce of 1,306 permanent employees as of 31st March 2026 (1,345 total employees including other-than-permanent), with women at 37.13% of permanent employees; permanent employee turnover was 17% in 2025-26 versus 13% in CY 2024.
- Women represent 14.29% of the Board of Directors, which includes one Woman Independent Director.
- Material responsible-business-conduct issues formally identified are Regulatory Compliance, Data Privacy and Business Ethics as risks, and Customer Satisfaction and Employees as opportunities.
- Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for all stakeholder groups, including a published Vigil Mechanism Policy for employees and workers and SEBI SCORES for investors and shareholders.
- Certification services — grading and certification of diamonds, colored stones and jewelry — account for 98.79% of turnover, so the reported sustainability footprint is service- and laboratory-based rather than manufacturing-based.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: IGI's expansion in 2025-26 was inorganic and footprint-led rather than plant-led, consistent with an asset-light laboratory model. The defining step was the completed acquisition of American Gemological Laboratories (AGL), described as a strategic expansion of the Company's global colored gemstone certification capabilities; the transaction combines IGI's global footprint, operational scale and infrastructure with AGL's established scientific expertise in colored gemstone analysis, strengthening IGI's presence in the United States — one of the largest markets for fine jewelry and colored gemstones — while reinforcing linkages with India as a key global hub for gemstone manufacturing, and is expected to deliver improved market access and operational synergies. The underlying platform being expanded is a network of 36 laboratories and 21 gemological schools spanning major jewelry hubs in India, USA, China, the UAE and Europe. No new laboratory construction project, commissioning date or capex programme is named in the routed sections; the only capital-deployment detail disclosed is that IPO proceeds were applied to the acquisition of the IGI Belgium Group and IGI Netherlands Group from the Promoter and to general corporate purposes, monitored by ICRA Limited. The remainder of the routed capacity narrative is industry rather than company capacity: Indian lab-grown diamond growers have increased capacity consistently, the domestic CVD reactor base is expanding, manufacturers are planning to double production capacity over the next three years to meet rising demand, and India accounts for roughly 35% of global rough LGD output and about 28.6% of global LGD exports. IGI positions itself as the beneficiary of that third-party capacity build-out, citing deep integration with key growers including in-factory grading, which provides visibility on rising volumes, and rising volumes plus operational efficiencies as the source of operating leverage.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Certification penetration, currently estimated at 65-70%, is expected to rise to 80-85% in the coming years, with significant headroom in smaller diamonds and finished jewelry.
- The shift from unorganised to branded diamond jewelry and the growth of organised retail and e-commerce is making certification an essential part of the purchase journey rather than a value-added service.
- Rapid rise of lab-grown diamonds is reshaping the industry's foundations and broadening the overall market by making diamond ownership accessible to a wider set of consumers.
- The global jewelry market, valued at approximately USD 243 billion, is projected to expand to nearly USD 387 billion by 2034, with diamonds expected to become the leading jewelry category.
- India's diamond share of the jewelry market has risen from around 7% in 2019 and is projected to reach 22-27% by 2029.
- India emerged as the world's second-largest diamond jewelry market in 2026, accounting for approximately 12% of global demand, and handles over 90% of global rough diamond polishing.
- India exported more polished lab-grown diamonds than natural diamonds over a full financial year for the first time, a structural shift in the industry.
- Operating leverage: as certification penetration increases, management sees a clear opportunity to expand reach while benefiting from operating leverage and sustained demand for services.
- Real GDP growth of approximately 7.6% in FY 2025-26 and the strongest private consumption cycle in more than a decade support premium and luxury demand in India, including fine jewelry.
- Headwind: subdued global demand, tariff-related uncertainties and rising bullion prices are near-term challenges for India's gem and jewelry sector.
- Headwind: sustained global uncertainty kept gold prices elevated, shifting consumer preference toward lighter, value-optimized designs and more accessible categories.
- Headwind: persistent geopolitical uncertainty — Russia-Ukraine, escalating tensions across West Asia and Red Sea disruptions — continues to impact global trade corridors and supply chain efficiency.
- Headwind: Middle East luxury demand shock, with regional luxury sales projected to decline by as much as 50% amid conflict and closure of critical transit hubs such as Dubai.
- The global luxury sector held at approximately EUR 1.44 trillion in CY 2025 and is expected to expand at 4-6% annually over the next decade, with jewelry leading category growth on emotional value and customisation.
- Technology-led investment cycle centred on artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in how gemstones and jewelry are graded, authenticated and certified.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Strong start to FY27: consolidated certification revenue +23% (volume +17%), EBITDA +29% (60.4% margin, +270 bps), PAT +31% — LGD (loose +25%, jewellery +44%) and the AGL coloured-stone consolidation (+200% gemstones) drive growth, while natural-diamond loose (+6%) is the strategic focus for share gains. The moat thesis holds: "an IGI certificate makes a lab-grown diamond a diamond" — grower capacity is doubling, and every stone needs certifying. Guidance (conservatively) held at 15% revenue / 20% EBITDA growth + AGL.

risks.note: Theft, fraud or damage to diamonds, jewelry and gemstones during certification or transportation could result in financial loss and reputational harm; mitigated through robust security systems, comprehensive insurance coverage and advanced tracking technologies.
risks.risk: Security and insurance risk over client goods in custody and transit

risks.note: Failure to adopt emerging technologies such as advanced spectroscopy, automation or AI could affect operational efficiency, competitiveness and market positioning. The BRSR additionally flags cybersecurity and data privacy as a material risk, where threats and system vulnerabilities could compromise the security, integrity and availability of client and company data.
risks.risk: Technological risk — failure to adopt emerging grading technology
